facts.statement: Dzharaonyx is a genus of alvarezsaurid theropod from the Late Cretaceous Bissekty Formation of Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: Dzharaonyx (meaning "Dzharakuduk claw", named after the type locality) is a genus of alvarezsaurid theropod from the Late Cretaceous Bissekty Formation of Uzbekistan.

facts.statement: The only known species of Dzharaonyx is D. eski.
facts.quote: The type and only species is D. eski.

facts.statement: The specific epithet "eski" means "old" in the Uzbek language.
facts.quote: The specific epithet "eski" is an Uzbek word for "old".

facts.statement: All remains of Dzharaonyx were found at the Dzharakuduk locality in the Kyzylkum Desert of Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: All remains of Dzharaonyx were discovered at a single locality called Dzharakuduk, which is in the Kyzylkum Desert of Uzbekistan.

facts.statement: Lev Nesov discovered the first alvarezsaurid remains that would later be classified as Dzharaonyx between 1977 and 1994.
facts.quote: The first remains belonging to alvarezsaurid dinosaurs, which would later be referred to Dzharaonyx were discovered by Lev Nesov during the period between 1977-1994

facts.statement: Additional remains were discovered between 1997 and 2006 by the URBAC joint-paleontological expedition.
facts.quote: Additional remains would be found in the period between 1997-2006 by the so-called "URBAC joint-paleontological expedition"

facts.statement: By 2017, only seven bones confidently identified as alvarezsaurs had been found among over 3,500 catalogued dinosaur fossils.
facts.quote: As of a 2017 publication, only seven bones confidently attributable to alvarezsaurs had been found out of over 3500 catalogued dinosaur fossils.

facts.statement: Dzharaonyx was formally named and described in 2022 by Alexander Averianov and Hans Dieter-Sues.
facts.quote: the taxon was not fully described and given a name until 2022 when Alexander Averianov and Hans Dieter-Sues published on it.

facts.statement: Dzharaonyx was a relatively small dinosaur, similar to other parvicursorines.
facts.quote: Dzharaonyx, like all parvicursorines, was a relatively small dinosaur.

facts.statement: Subsequent researchers estimated Dzharaonyx was about 50 cm long and weighed approximately 1.75 kg.
facts.quote: subsequent researchers have estimated that it was around the same size as Linhenykus at around 50 cm long and weighing around 1.75 kg.

facts.statement: Dzharaonyx is distinguished by unique features such as opisthocoelous dorsal vertebrae, a large olecranon process, an arctometatarsus, and small flexor tubercles on its toe claws.
facts.quote: Dzharaonyx is able to be distinguished from all other alvarezsaurids by the following autapomorphies: opisthocoelous dorsal vertebrae lacking a fossa between the zygapopyses, procoelous caudal vertebrae with a canal inside the neural arch, a small tuberosity inside the humerus, a radial condyle that protrudes outwardly, a very large olecranon process of the ulna, globular-shaped trochlea on the carpometacarpus, a lack of a process on top of the second manual phalanges, a tubercle just in front of the acetabulum, an arctometatarsus, a flange on the outside of the second metatarsal, and small flexor tubercles on the toe claws.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Dzharaonyx within the monophyletic subfamily Parvicursorinae.
facts.quote: When Averianov and Sues described Dzharaonyx in 2022, they conducted a phylogenetic analysis which recovered Dzharaonyx within a monophyletic Parvicursorinae.

facts.statement: Dzharaonyx represents the oldest known record of Parvicursorinae, suggesting an Asian origin for the group.
facts.quote: Dzharaonyx therefore represents the oldest record of Parvicursorinae anywhere in the world, supporting an Asian origin for the group.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Dzharaonyx's small size reflects a "miniaturization event" in alvarezsaurian evolution during the early-to-middle Cenomanian.
facts.quote: They found Dzharaonyx as a member of Parvicursorinae and suggested that its appearance is reflective of a "miniaturization event" within alvarezsaurian evolution that occurred during the early-to-middle Cenomanian.

facts.statement: Geological evidence indicates that a braided river system replaced the coastline in the environment where Dzharaonyx lived.
facts.quote: The geology of the formations indicates that a braided river system took the place of the coastline.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Dzharaonyx may have specialized in feeding on colonial insects like ants due to its hand morphology and the spread of angiosperms.
facts.quote: These simultaneous developments, coupled with the unique morphology of alvarezsaurid hands, has been used to suggest that they may have been specialized to feed on colonial insects like ants.

facts.statement: The Dzharakuduk locality also yielded fossils of Timurlengia, Bissektipelta, Ulughbegsaurus, enantiornithines, and amphibians.
facts.quote: The locality from which Dzharaonyx was unearthed, Dzharakuduk, has yielded fossils from other dinosaurs including the tyrannosauroid Timurlengia, the ankylosaur Bissektipelta, and the probable carcharodontosaurid Ulughbegsaurus, as well as fossils from enantiornithines and amphibians.

facts.statement: The genus Dzharaonyx was named by Averianov and Sues in 2022.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Averianov & Sues, 2022
